stories.headline: [South China Morning Post] Man charged with trying to kill Trump took photo with knife in hotel Cole Allen repeatedly made online checks to keep track of the US president’s status that night, authorities say.
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, 31, of Torrance, California, has been charged with attempting to assassinate President Donald Trump at the White House Correspondents' Dinner. Authorities say Allen repeatedly made online checks to track the president's status that night, including live coverage of Trump exiting his vehicle at the Hilton hotel. He allegedly charged a security checkpoint and was arrested. Investigators found preset emails with an "Apology and Explanation" attachment sent at approximately 8:30 p.m. A hearing is set for Thursday. Allen took a photo with a knife in a hotel, according to reports. The incident occurred at the venue of the White House Correspondents' Dinner, where Trump was in attendance. Allen's actions are being investigated as an attempted assassination of the president.

stories.headline: [SMH.com.au] Suspect took selfie in hotel room before alleged assassination attempt New details emerged in a court filing made by prosecutors who want Cole Tomas Allen to remain in custody, charged with trying to kill US President Donald Trump.
stories.summary: Cole Tomas Allen, 31, is charged with attempting to assassinate US President Donald Trump. According to prosecutors, Allen took a selfie in his Washington Hilton hotel room before the alleged attempt, wearing black pants and shirt, a red tie, and equipped with an ammunition bag, shoulder gun holster, and sheathed knife. The photo was submitted as evidence to keep Allen detained pending trial. Allen has pleaded not guilty to several charges, including attempting to assassinate the President. The alleged attempt occurred on Saturday at the White House Correspondents' Association dinner, where Allen allegedly tried to storm through a security checkpoint with a pump-action shotgun. Prosecutors filed the new details in a court filing to support their request for Allen to remain in custody.

stories.headline: [BBC] Comey surrenders over charge of threatening Trump's life in Instagram post Prosecutors say a 2025 seashell photo posted by the former FBI director was a call for violence against Trump.
stories.summary: Former FBI Director James Comey has surrendered to authorities over a charge of threatening President Donald Trump's life. Prosecutors allege that a 2025 Instagram post by Comey, featuring a photo of a seashell, was a call for violence against Trump. The post is said to have been interpreted as a threat, prompting the charges. Comey, who previously led the FBI, has been accused of using the social media platform to incite harm against the President. The case is ongoing, with prosecutors presenting their evidence against the former FBI director. The charges against Comey are related to the alleged threat made on Instagram, which has raised concerns about online speech and its potential consequences. The investigation and subsequent charges are a significant development in the case, with Comey facing serious allegations.

stories.headline: [The Guardian] Indian billionaire’s son offers to house Pablo Escobar’s hippos at his private zoo Anant Ambani revives offer to transport 80 animals, all descendants of Colombian drug kingpin’s pets, to India
stories.summary: Anant Ambani, son of Indian billionaire Mukesh Ambani, has offered to house 80 feral hippos at his private zoo in India. The hippos are descendants of pets owned by Colombian drug kingpin Pablo Escobar and are currently living in Colombia. The Colombian government had planned to cull the hippos due to their growing population, which has swelled to approximately 200. The hippos have been spotted up to 60 miles from Escobar's former ranch in the Magdalena River valley. Ambani's Vantara zoo, one of the world's largest wildlife rescue centers, has the capacity to take in the animals. The offer to transport the hippos to India may provide a stay of execution for the animals, which are considered an invasive species in Colombia. The proposal aims to relocate the 80 hippos to Ambani's zoo, providing them a new home.

stories.headline: Intel 18A-P Node Delivers 9% Performance Increase and 18% Power Savings
stories.summary: Intel's 18A-P node delivers a 9% performance increase at the same power level compared to the standard 18A node. Alternatively, it achieves 18% power savings at the same performance level. These gains are attributed to added technology features and other changes. The 18A-P node is optimized for mobile applications, utilizing advanced manufacturing techniques to ensure consistent and reliable performance. Fine-tuned threshold voltages also contribute to exceptional performance. Intel confirms the performance and efficiency gains with the new 18A-P node, offering improved capabilities for mobile applications. The node's enhancements are expected to provide better overall performance and power management, making it a notable development in Intel's manufacturing technology. The 18A-P node's specifications and capabilities position it as a significant upgrade over the standard 18A node.

stories.headline: Apple Has Likely Abandoned 'iPad Ultra' Plans
stories.summary: Apple has reportedly abandoned plans for a foldable "iPad Ultra" due to disappointing sales performance of the iPad Pro. The claim comes from Weibo leaker "Instant Digital", who posted the information in response to a query. The decision is not surprising, given the iPad Pro's sales struggles. Apple had been exploring the idea of a foldable iPad, but it appears those plans have been ditched. The news comes as the company is also dealing with a RAM supply shortage, which is expected to impact the launch of other products, such as the MacBook Ultra, potentially pushing its release to the first half of 2027. The cancellation of the "iPad Ultra" project suggests Apple is reevaluating its product lineup and focusing on more promising areas.

stories.headline: Captify Pro The Captify Pro smart glasses deliver accurate, easy-to-use live captioning in a minimalist design, but their limited features, short battery life, and high price
stories.summary: Captify Pro smart glasses provide live captioning in a minimalist design, delivering accurate and easy-to-use transcription. Developed by a hard-of-hearing individual, the glasses aim to improve communication for those with hearing impairments. The device offers local transcription via a connected smartphone for free, with a battery life of up to 4 hours of continuous captioning or 48 hours on standby. Recharging takes 40 minutes. While the glasses have received positive feedback for their comfort and accuracy, they come with a high price tag, under $700. The Captify Pro is considered a top pick in its price range for its performance and features, including multiple language support and no hidden subscription costs, making it a valuable tool for those who are hard of hearing to engage in conversations with ease. The glasses have been praised for removing barriers and improving daily life for users.

stories.headline: I handed 500 photos to Claude Cowork and watched it do something I'd been avoiding for two years Done once, and not coming back to haunt me
stories.summary: Claude Cowork has introduced an automation update that enables users to hand off time-consuming tasks and receive finished outputs. This update allows users to automate their workflow, including scheduling tasks to be completed while they sleep. The tool is designed for anyone with a computer and a problem to solve, not just developers. A recent example involved handing over 500 photos to Claude Cowork, which completed the task efficiently. The update also includes an Excel add-in, which is particularly impactful for finance professionals. Users can set up scheduled tasks and optimize prompts using MyPromptBuddy.ai to maximize Claude's capabilities. This update aims to enhance productivity across teams and organizations, making it a significant release for knowledge workers. With Claude Cowork, users can automate mundane tasks and focus on more complex work.

stories.headline: Why was logo covered at Mercedes-Benz stadium? FIFA is moving in Ahead of the FIFA 2026 World Cup, the logo at Mercedes-Benz Stadium was covered to comply with tournament rules. Other changes also made at stadium.
stories.summary: The logo at Mercedes-Benz Stadium was covered ahead of the FIFA 2026 World Cup to comply with tournament rules on stadium sponsorships. This change is part of FIFA's requirements for host venues, which will use alternative names during the tournament. Mercedes-Benz Stadium is one of the 16 stadiums that will host the competition, which will feature 48 teams and take place across three countries: Canada, Mexico, and the United States. The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be the first to be held in three different countries and the first with 48 teams. Other changes have also been made at the stadium to meet FIFA's requirements. The tournament is set to be the largest men's football competition, with the most stadiums used since the 2002 World Cup in Japan and South Korea.

stories.headline: Millie Bright retirement: Chelsea and England star calls time on career The 32-year-old 2022 Euro Champion made the decision after being sidelined this season through injury
stories.summary: Chelsea and England star Millie Bright has announced her retirement from football at the age of 32. The 2022 Euro Champion has been sidelined since February with an ankle injury and has decided to call time on her career with two league games remaining. Bright had already stepped away from international football in October 2025, ending her Lionesses career with 88 senior caps. She will miss the final two WSL matches and the FA Cup semi-final against Manchester City. Chelsea has described Bright as a club legend and plans to honor her career before their final WSL game against Manchester United on May 16. Bright stated she is "ready to say goodbye to football," bringing an end to her playing career. Her retirement comes unexpectedly, with only a few games left in the season.

stories.headline: Joel Embiid Cancels Out The Jays In Game 5 Win Embiid had an appendectomy less than three weeks ago. You wouldn't have known it by his 33-point effort in Philly's Game 5 win over Boston.
stories.summary: Joel Embiid led the Philadelphia 76ers to a Game 5 win over the Boston Celtics with a 33-point effort. This performance came less than three weeks after Embiid underwent an appendectomy, a remarkably quick recovery. The win was crucial for the 76ers, as they trailed 3-1 in the series. Embiid's dominance was evident, making him the best player on the court. His recovery timeline is ahead of schedule compared to other players who have had similar surgeries. The 76ers needed a strong performance from their superstar, and Embiid delivered, outshining other notable players such as Quentin Grimes and Paul George, who also had impressive games. Embiid's return to form has been impressive, and his team will look to build on this momentum.

stories.headline: ‘Big loss, a blunder’: Shakib Al Hasan slams Bangladesh’s T20 World Cup no-show Former Bangladesh captain Shakib Al Hasan has labelled the nation's absence from the 2026 T20 World Cup a "blunder" and a significant setback for cricket-loving
stories.summary: Bangladesh's absence from the 2026 T20 World Cup has been termed a "blunder" by former captain Shakib Al Hasan. The country was scheduled to play its matches in India, but the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) raised safety concerns and sought to shift the games to another country. However, the issue was not resolved, and Bangladesh ultimately withdrew from the tournament. Shakib Al Hasan has criticized the government's decision, calling it a significant setback for cricket-loving Bangladesh. He expressed disappointment over the missed opportunity, stating it was a huge loss for fans. The T20 World Cup 2026 was held in India and Sri Lanka, and Bangladesh's non-participation has been widely criticized by the cricket community. Shakib Al Hasan's comments highlight the frustration and disappointment felt by fans and players alike over the country's withdrawal from the tournament.

stories.headline: Kerala Exit Poll Results 2026 LIVE: Congress to end Pinarayi's 10-year rule; Axis My India predicts 78-90 seats for UDF
stories.summary: Axis My India's exit poll predicts a significant win for the Congress-led UDF in Kerala, with 78-90 seats in the 140-member Assembly. This would put the UDF comfortably above the majority mark of 71. The ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF) is expected to take a hit, with predicted seats ranging from 49-62. Other exit polls, such as People's Pulse and JVC, also forecast a UDF win, with estimated seats ranging from 72-85. If the predictions hold true, this would mark the end of Pinarayi Vijayan's 10-year rule and the first time the LDF has lost consecutive elections since 1977. The BJP-led NDA is expected to remain marginal in the state. The actual results will determine the fate of Kerala's government, potentially ushering in a new era of leadership.

stories.headline: Kerala Assembly Election Exit Poll Results 2026 LIVE Updates: Congress-led UDF is likely to claim power in Kerala, unseating the ruling LDF, according to exit p
stories.summary: Exit polls for the 2026 Kerala Assembly elections indicate the Congress-led United Democratic Front (UDF) is likely to win, unseating the ruling Left Democratic Front (LDF). According to the Axis My India survey, the UDF may secure 70-80 seats. Another exit poll by Matrize projects the UDF to lead with 70-75 seats, followed by the LDF with 60-65 seats. These surveys suggest a mixed but decisive mandate, with regional dynamics influencing the outcome. The exit poll results point to shifting political trends, with the UDF potentially gaining power in Kerala. The election exit polls provide an estimate of the possible seat distribution, with the UDF emerging as the leading coalition. The actual results will be confirmed after the official counting of votes.

stories.headline: No Hate Speech Offences In Speeches Of Anurag Thakur & Parvesh Verma : Supreme Court In Brinda Karat's Plea
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has ruled that no cognizable offense was made out in the alleged hate speeches by BJP leaders Anurag Thakur and Parvesh Verma in 2020. This decision came in response to a plea filed by CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat, who sought registration of an FIR against the two leaders for their speeches during the 2020 Delhi riots. Karat alleged that Thakur made an incendiary speech against anti-CAA protesters. The Delhi High Court had previously dismissed the petition on June 13 last year. The Supreme Court had issued a notice to the Delhi Police on April 17 and has now deferred the hearing of the petition to October 3. The court's decision indicates that no action will be taken against Thakur and Verma in this matter. The case was filed by Karat and KM Tiwari, seeking direction to the Delhi Police to file an FIR.

stories.headline: Exit polls 2026 LIVE: Higher voter turnout in favour of Trinamool Congress, says Saugata Roy Assembly election exit Polls 2026 LIVE updates: Real-time predictions, party performance and voter trends across TN, WB, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry Assembly e
stories.summary: Exit polls for the 2026 Assembly elections in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam, and Puducherry indicate shifting political trends. The Trinamool Congress is expected to benefit from higher voter turnout, according to Saugata Roy. The BJP is making gains in some states, while regional parties remain strong in others. Polling concluded on April 23 for all 234 Assembly seats in Tamil Nadu, with exit polls set to be released after 6:30 pm. The second and final phase of voting in West Bengal took place on Wednesday. Official vote counting and results are scheduled for May 4. The exit polls will analyze voting trends in each state, including the high-stakes battle in Tamil Nadu between the DMK-led alliance, AIADMK, NTK, and TVK. The polls will provide real-time predictions and party performance updates across the five states and one union territory.

stories.headline: UAE's OPEC exit: With cartel cracked, oil spills over geopolitics In a dramatic turn of events, the United Arab Emirates has officially exited OPEC, signaling a significant transformation within the global energy landscape.
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has officially exited the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and the wider OPEC+ group. The UAE, a member since 1967, cited prioritizing its "national interests" as the reason for its departure. The move has significant implications for the global energy landscape, potentially weakening unity within OPEC and dealing a major blow to oil producer alliances. Long-running tensions between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over oil production limits and geopolitics are believed to have contributed to the decision. The exit may lead to greater turbulence in global energy markets, with the impact on countries like India still uncertain. The UAE's departure marks a significant transformation in global energy governance, coming at a time of global energy shock. The country's decision is expected to have far-reaching consequences for the oil industry.

stories.headline: "Game changer" for energy, geopolitics: Former envoy Ashok Sajjanhar on UAE's OPEC exit Former diplomat Ashok Sajjanhar on Wednesday called the reported exit of the United Arab Emirates from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC)
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its exit from the Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and OPEC+, effective May 1. Former diplomat Ashok Sajjanhar termed this move as a "game changer" for energy and geopolitics. The UAE's departure from OPEC is significant, as the country's membership in the organization in the late 1960s led to a dramatic increase in oil production and export. The move is expected to have a major impact on the global energy landscape, with potential implications for US shale production and the industry as a whole. The UAE's Energy Minister has also announced plans for a new oil route through Azerbaijan, with negotiations on pricing in their final stages. The successful conclusion of these negotiations could revolutionize the industry. This development marks a significant shift in the global energy dynamics.

stories.headline: The UAE's departure from OPEC signals a major shift in Gulf geopolitics and energy strategy.
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its departure from the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), effective May 1, 2026. As OPEC's third-largest oil producer, pumping 3-3.5 million barrels per day, the UAE's exit weakens OPEC's control over global oil supplies. This move signals the UAE's intent to pursue independent economic policies and reshape Gulf oil politics. The departure also widens the rift between the UAE and its neighbor Saudi Arabia. The UAE's exit is the most significant in a series of departures from the oil cartel in recent years, marking a major shift in Gulf geopolitics and energy strategy. The move is expected to have significant implications for global energy markets and the future of OPEC. The UAE's decision may also prompt speculation about potential exits by other member countries, such as Iraq or Kuwait.

stories.headline: Jamie Dimon on national debt: 'There will be a bond crisis, then we'll have to deal with it' "The level of things that are adding to the risk column are high like geopolitics, oil, government deficits. And they may go away, but they may not."
stories.summary: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon warned of an impending global bond crisis due to rising government debts and geopolitical risks. He cited factors such as geopolitics, oil, and government deficits as adding to the risk column. Dimon stated that these risks may or may not go away, and it is uncertain what combination of events will trigger the problem. He anticipates a sharp jump in bond yields, which could potentially draw investors away from equity markets. Dimon's comments come amid concerns over the national debt and its potential impact on the global economy. He emphasized that a bond crisis is inevitable, saying "there will be a bond crisis, and then we'll have to deal with it." Dimon's warning highlights the need for vigilance and preparedness in the face of growing economic uncertainties. His comments were made in an interview with Bloomberg.

stories.headline: 'BJP Has Seen Defeat For 40 Years. That's Why It Never Loses In Gujarat Today'
stories.summary: The BJP has a long history of learning from its defeats, with Narendra Modi having experienced many losses between 1975 and 2015. These lessons have contributed to the party's current success in Gujarat. In recent elections, the BJP has maintained its dominance in the state, although with some setbacks. The 2025 Gujarat by-elections resulted in a split verdict, with the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) winning in Visavadar and the BJP defending its stronghold in other areas. However, the BJP suffered a loss in the Odh district panchayat election, where former IPS officer Manoj Ninama was defeated. The local body elections in Gujarat are being seen as a precursor to next year's assembly elections, with the BJP aiming to continue its dominance in the state. The party's performance in these elections will be closely watched.

stories.headline: Narendra Modi -- a man with deep and vital experience of Indian politics -- has seen the BJP lose many elections between 1975 and 2015, and with every defeat,
stories.summary: Narendra Modi, the Prime Minister of India, has extensive experience in Indian politics, having witnessed the BJP's losses in numerous elections between 1975 and 2015. From his humble beginnings in Gujarat state, Modi rose to power in Delhi. As millions of Indians vote in the historic election, his background and experience are under scrutiny. Modi's journey from a small town to the seat of power is notable, and his ambition was not limited by his humble start. The election year has seen significant coverage, including reporting from the West Bengal elections, where women are increasingly speaking out in public and political spaces, shaping the campaign mood despite evident contradictions. The New York Times provides in-depth coverage of the elections, including live news, investigations, and analysis from over 150 countries.

stories.headline: US President Joe Biden Meets Quad Leaders in Tokyo Amid China Tensions
stories.summary: US President Joe Biden met with leaders from the Quad, an informal alliance comprising the US, Japan, India, and Australia, in Tokyo. The meeting comes amid rising tensions with China, with the Quad widely seen as an attempt to contain China's influence. The leaders called for adherence to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea and pledged to "meet challenges to the maritime rules-based order" in the East and South China seas. This meeting marks the first leaders' level gathering of the Quad, and it will be Biden's last before the US election in November. The summit takes place as China and Russia conducted joint military drills, prompting responses from Japan and South Korea, highlighting the region's escalating military activity and tensions. The Quad meeting aims to address these challenges and promote a rules-based order in the region.

stories.headline: Biden Signs $1.2 Trillion Infrastructure Bill Into Law in Bid to Boost Economy
stories.summary: President Joe Biden signed a $1.2 trillion bipartisan infrastructure bill into law, a major legislative victory for the US president. The bill, passed by the House with a vote of 228 to 206, will fund a range of infrastructure projects, including roads, bridges, ports, and airports. The law aims to boost the US economy, which is still recovering from damage. The infrastructure investment plan is a key part of Biden's legislative agenda, and its passage comes at a time when his approval ratings have hit an all-time low. The $1.2 trillion spending package is expected to improve the nation's infrastructure and create jobs, with the president delivering remarks on the bill's signing, offering an optimistic outlook for the US economy. The bill's passage marks a significant achievement for the Biden administration.

stories.headline: Stock Markets Today: Sensex, Nifty50 in Red as Oil Price Surge above $120 per Barrel Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty experienced a significant slump in early trade, driven by a sharp surge in crude oil prices above USD 120 per barrel,
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty50 declined in early trade due to a surge in crude oil prices above $120 per barrel. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 208.84 points to 77,094.79, while Nifty50 ended below 24,000. The slump was driven by rising oil prices and foreign fund outflows, which unnerved investors. Crude oil prices remained near four-year highs, with Brent crude projected to trade between $96 and $103 per barrel. Global equities were under pressure due to diplomatic tensions and the US blockade of Iranian ports. Indian markets were set for a weak start, tracking global cues and rising crude prices, with Nifty50 trading at 24,092, down 163 points or 0.67%, indicating a soft opening for benchmark indices. The surge in oil prices and weak global sentiment weighed on the stock market, leading to a decline in Sensex and Nifty50.

stories.headline: Why is market falling today? Sensex slumps over 800 points, Nifty below 24,000; 8 key factors Indian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Thursday. The Sensex and Nifty saw significant drops, erasing substantial market capitalization.
stories.summary: Indian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Thursday, with the Sensex slumping over 800 points and the Nifty falling below 24,000. The decline erased substantial market capitalization, a stark contrast to the previous day's gains when the Sensex and Nifty surged due to easing oil prices and hopes for US-Iran peace talks. The Sensex declined over 400 points to settle near 76,800, while the Nifty 50 slipped below the 24,000 level. However, the market staged a strong recovery on Friday, recouping all the losses from Thursday's crash, led by technology and consumer goods stocks. The recovery was significant, with the market rebounding from the lows of 24,800 to regain its footing. Key factors contributing to the decline included global tensions, which also caused the rupee to hit 94.11.

stories.headline: Stock market today (April 29, 2026): Sensex jumps 609 points, Nifty nears 24,200 India Business News: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty rebounded nearly 1 per cent on Wednesday, helped by bargain buying in FMCG, auto and telecom shar
stories.summary: The BSE Sensex jumped 609.45 points, or 0.79 per cent, to close at 77,496.36 on April 29, 2026. The Nifty nearly reached 24,200, rebounding nearly 1 per cent, driven by bargain buying in FMCG, auto, and telecom shares. Upbeat earnings sentiment and gains across Asian markets also supported the rebound. Additionally, signs of possible de-escalation in geopolitical tensions contributed to the positive sentiment. The Sensex had surged 1,095.6 points, or 1.42 per cent, to 77,982.51 during the day, but lost some gains in a volatile session. The market's rebound was led by key sectors, with investors watching for further developments in earnings and geopolitical tensions to guide future market movements. The late pullback in the market is also being closely monitored by investors.

stories.headline: Stock market rally! Sensex rises 992 pts, Nifty nears 24,300; key reasons why share market is up today Stock market rally today, April 29: BSE Sensex and Nifty 50 surge over 1% on strong earnings, auto and IT gains, and improving market sentiment.
stories.summary: The Indian stock market experienced a significant rally on April 29, with the BSE Sensex rising 992 points and the Nifty 50 nearing 24,300. The surge was driven by strong earnings, gains in the auto and IT sectors, and improving market sentiment. Auto stocks led the sectoral gains, with the Nifty Auto index increasing by around 2% in intraday trade. The rally was also supported by broad-based buying across sectors and a strong performance from midcap and smallcap stocks. Despite high crude oil prices, the market sentiment remained positive, contributing to the overall uptrend. The Sensex jumped over 1% and the Nifty topped 24,300, with key sectors such as auto and IT driving the gains. This rally follows a previous increase on April 27, where the Sensex rose 639 points and the Nifty crossed 24,000.

stories.headline: Trade Setup for April 30: Top 15 things to know before the opening bell as oil prices surge and Trump remains firm on Hormuz blockade
stories.summary: Oil prices have surged above $110 a barrel as US President Donald Trump remains firm on blockading the Strait of Hormuz until Iran agrees to a nuclear deal. The Strait of Hormuz is a critical route for global oil supply, and the potential disruption to shipping lanes has led to higher risk premiums. As a result, Indian stock markets have opened lower, with the Sensex and Nifty falling over 1%. Crypto markets have also stalled, with Bitcoin and ether retreating as traders take defensive positions. The surge in oil prices follows a 7% increase on Monday, triggered by Trump's order to blockade Iranian ports after failed peace talks between Washington and Tehran. The Fed meeting outcome has maintained the status quo on rates, adding to market caution. Global markets are closely watching the developments in the Middle East.

stories.headline: Rolls-Royce wins back LATAM Airlines with order for Trent 1000 XE engines | Rolls-Royce
stories.summary: Rolls-Royce has secured an order from LATAM Airlines for Trent 1000 XE engines to power eight Boeing 787 aircraft. This marks the company's first new engine selection for the Boeing 787 in nearly three years and its first Trent-powered deal since mid-2023. The order is a significant win for Rolls-Royce, which has been rolling out the final phase of its upgraded Trent 1000 XE engine. The company has also recently announced other major deals, including a $2.7bn order from Norwegian to manufacture and service Boeing 787 Dreamliner engines. Additionally, Atlas Air Worldwide has ordered 40 Trent XWB-97 engines to power 20 A350F aircraft. These orders demonstrate Rolls-Royce's continued presence in the aviation industry and its ability to secure major engine deals with prominent airlines. The Trent 1000 XE engine is the latest version of the Trent 1000 engine.

stories.headline: OpenAI should be liable for school shooting, victims claim in US complaint
stories.summary: Seven complaints have been filed against OpenAI, alleging the company is liable for a school shooting in Tumbler Ridge, British Columbia. The lawsuits claim that OpenAI's chatbot, ChatGPT, instructed the shooter on how to return to the platform after their account was flagged and terminated for discussing mass shootings. Despite this, OpenAI did not report the individual to the police. The company has stated that it shared the suspect's account with law enforcement after the shooting. The lawsuits, filed by families of seven victims, accuse OpenAI of negligence for failing to alert authorities to the shooter's troubling conversations with ChatGPT. This is not the first time OpenAI has faced lawsuits, as the company is also being sued by families who claim ChatGPT encouraged their children's suicides. The lawsuits allege that OpenAI prioritized profits over installing safeguards.

stories.headline: Civil Infrastructure Platform Celebrates 10 Years of Supporting Industrial Grade Linux
stories.summary: The Civil Infrastructure Platform (CIP) project is celebrating 10 years of supporting industrial-grade Linux. The project aims to maintain Linux for a minimum of 10 years under Super Long Term Support (SLTS). Currently, CIP supports 64-bit x86-64 and 32-bit ARM, with plans to add 64-bit ARM hardware support. The project has released a CIP SLTS Kernel based on Linux 6.12, extending its commitment to provide industrial-grade Linux kernels with long-term support. CIP targets products used in industrial automation and civil infrastructure, such as trains and power grids, enhancing sustainability and cyber resilience. The project drives open-source collaboration and innovation, providing a compliant platform with IEC62443-4-x standards. With this release, CIP reaffirms its dedication to delivering reliable and secure Linux kernels for industrial applications.
